section_about:
OpenAI's Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems.
We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.
We are looking for customer-focused software engineers to build effective custom software that leverages OpenAI's APIs to solve real customer problems.
As an FDSWE, you will work with our customers and OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers to design and implement scalable solutions that solve their most difficult problems.

You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architects, and Customer Success Managers who work on the same account.

OpenAI's Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems.
We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.
Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change.
We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact-not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

section_about:
OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems.
The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.
The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.
We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design and integrate power-generation and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses.
You will work across prime movers, fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, water treatment, heat recovery, acoustics, fire interfaces, and plant auxiliaries.
The role combines first-principles engineering with practical vendor and field execution to deliver systems that are safe, efficient, maintainable, and ready for demanding operating profiles.
Travel: 50%
section_responsibilities:
- Develop mechanical basis-of-design documents, process flow diagrams, P&IDs, specifications, calculations, and equipment requirements for power generation facilities.
- Design and review prime-mover auxiliaries, fuel gas or liquid fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, lubrication, compressed air, water treatment, and heat-recovery systems.
- Evaluate thermal performance, hydraulic behavior, pressure drop, vibration, acoustics, emissions interfaces, redundancy, and maintenance requirements.
- Translate generation duty cycles and data center load profiles into equipment sizing, operating envelopes, and control requirements.
- Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment selections, test plans, failure modes, service strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.
- Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.
- Coordinate interfaces with electrical, controls, CSA, fuel supply, environmental, fire protection, and data center mechanical teams.
- Create repeatable mechanical reference designs and standards for future generation deployments.
section_requirements:
- 8+ years of mechanical engineering experience on power generation, oil and gas, industrial utilities, central plants, or mission-critical projects.
- Strong knowledge of rotating equipment, piping, heat transfer, fluid systems, thermal performance, ventilation, and mechanical auxiliaries.
- Experience with combined heat and power, heat recovery, modular generation, or microgrids.
- Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, generators, or comparable large industrial equipment.
- Ability to evaluate vendor data, equipment curves, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance constraints.
- Experience carrying designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and performance validation.
- Knowledge of applicable ASME, API, NFPA, ASHRAE, and environmental requirements.
- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.
section_preferred:
- Professional Engineer license.
- Experience with process simulation, hydraulic modeling, CFD, or equipment-performance modeling.
- Experience supporting high-density data center loads and rapid infrastructure deployment.

job_title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer - Foundations, Search
section_about:
The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI.
Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models.
Pushing the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, and efficiency improvements to propel our science.
The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack (serving, indexing, retrieval) to translate model intent into reliable, real-world actions.
Operating at the frontier of AI and information retrieval, the team develops large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to reason over global knowledge and act dependably.
In close partnership with researchers, we rapidly bring modeling breakthroughs into production and redefine how intelligent systems discover, retrieve, and synthesize information at planetary scale.
We're looking for a researcher focused on our search efforts.
You'll work with a a team of world-class research scientists and engineers developing foundational technology that enables models to retrieve and condition on the right information, at the right time.
This includes designing new embedding training objectives, scalable vector store architectures, and dynamic indexing methods.
This work will support retrieval across many OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication and deep technical impact.
section_responsibilities:
- Tackle embedding models and retrieval systems optimized for grounding, relevance, and adaptive reasoning.
- Collaborate with a team of researchers and engineers building end-to-end infrastructure for training, evaluating, and integrating embeddings into frontier models.
- Drive innovation in dense, sparse, and hybrid representation techniques, metric learning, and learning-to-retrieve systems.
- Collaborate closely with Pretraining, Inference, and other Research teams to integrate retrieval throughout the model lifecycle
- Contribute to OpenAI's long-term vision of AI systems with memory and knowledge access capabilities rooted in learned representations.
section_requirements:
- Proven experience leading high-performance teams of researchers or engineers in ML infrastructure or foundational research.
- Deep technical expertise in representation learning, embedding models, or vector retrieval systems.
- Familiarity with transformer-based LLMs and how embedding spaces can interact with language model objectives.
- Research experience in areas such as contrastive learning, supervised or unsupervised embedding learning, or metric learning.
- A track record of building or scaling large machine learning systems, particularly embedding pipelines in production or research contexts.
- A first-principles mindset for challenging assumptions about how retrieval and memory should work for large models.

section_about:
Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI's API platform.
These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world.
We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for.
Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.
We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering.
These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.
That reach creates challenging engineering problems.
We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change.
The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.
Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for.
The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.
We're hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience.
Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.
- Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.
- Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.
- Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.
- Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.
- Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.
- Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.
- Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.
- Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.
section_preferred:
- Experience with payments, subscriptions, pricing, billing, or other systems that manage customer purchases and revenue.
- Experience with product catalogs, packaging and bundles, workspace management, entitlements, or usage metering.
- Experience building financial or transaction systems at scale, checking that records match across systems, or supporting compliance and audits.

We act as trusted technical partners, guiding engineering teams as they integrate Codex into their projects and workflows.
Our customers span digital-native companies to global enterprises, and we work side-by-side to accelerate how they plan, build, and deliver software.
We are seeking a technically deep, creativity-driven Applied AI Engineer who is already a power user of AI coding tools and passionate about pushing the boundaries of developer productivity.
You will partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on builders to design, validate, and scale advanced AI workflows, often using Codex to prototype and build the very demos, integrations, and automations customers ultimately adopt.
This is a highly cross-functional role that blends technical architecture, product strategy, and customer-facing leadership.
You'll work closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Applied Engineering, and the broader Codex organization to advocate for customer needs, shape product direction, and accelerate the successful deployment of intelligent coding systems across some of the world's most influential companies.
This role is based in Singapore.

- Partner directly with customers to design and implement AI-enhanced development workflows, from rapid prototyping through scalable production rollout.
- Build high-quality demos, reference implementations, and workflow automations, using Codex itself as part of your development process.
- Lead large-format workshops, technical deep dives, and hands-on enablement sessions that help engineering organizations adopt AI coding tools effectively and safely.
- Contribute technical content including examples, guides, patterns, and best practices to the OpenAI Cookbook to help the broader developer community accelerate their work with Codex.
- Gather high-fidelity product insights from real customer deployments and translate them into clear product proposals and model feedback for internal teams.

section_about:
Security is at the foundation of OpenAI's mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.
The Security team protects OpenAI's technology, people, and products.
We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI.
Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.
As a Security Engineer, Application Security you will be responsible for identifying and mitigating security vulnerabilities within software applications through building security tools, code reviews, penetration testing, and security assessments.
We're looking for people who will work closely with development teams to ensure secure coding practices are integrated throughout the software development lifecycle, preventing security risks before they emerge.
You will also provide security guidance to developers and other stakeholders, fostering a culture of security awareness within the organization.
The role is preferred to be based in San Francisco, Seattle or New York City but may consider remote work.
section_responsibilities:
- Perform Security Assessments: Conduct regular security assessments, code reviews, and penetration testing to identify vulnerabilities in applications and software.
- Develop and Implement Security Tools: Design, develop, and implement security tools, frameworks, and methodologies to protect applications against security threats.
- Collaborate with Development Teams: Work closely with development teams to ensure security best practices are integrated throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC), including secure coding guidelines.
- Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment: Conduct threat modeling and risk assessments to proactively identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies.
- Vulnerability Management: Track, analyze, and manage vulnerabilities in applications, providing guidance and support for remediation efforts.
- Incident Response Support: Assist in investigating, analyzing, and responding to security incidents related to applications, ensuring timely resolution and documentation of incidents.
- Stay Current on Security Trends: Continuously stay updated on the latest security threats, vulnerabilities, and technologies to enhance security measures in applications.
section_requirements:
- Extensive experience in information security, cybersecurity, or a related field, with a significant portion of that experience in leadership or management roles.
- Deep understanding of security technologies, tools, and best practices, including experience with secure coding practices, threat modeling, risk assessments, and incident response.
- Experience in application security, software development, or related areas with a strong understanding of secure coding practices and application security frameworks.
- Proficiency in programming languages (such as Python, Java, C++, etc.), knowledge of security tools (e.g., Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP), and familiarity with security protocols and encryption methods.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex security issues to both technical and non-technical audiences

section_about:
Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings.
Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors.
We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples' lives.
As a Test Engineer on the Robotics team, you will help shape the next generation of embodied AI.
You'll design and run rigorous, exploratory and requirements-driven tests-building custom test equipment, analyzing results, and translating findings into actionable insights that drive design breakthroughs and mitigate risks across hardware and software.
This role offers the opportunity to directly influence how our AI scales beyond simulation, ensuring that every design, test, and iteration brings us closer to truly adaptive, versatile robotic systems.
section_responsibilities:
- Design and build custom test benches to evaluate system performance under realistic operating conditions; proficient in CAD and familiar with GD&T.
- Analyze and interpret test data to identify trends, anomalies, and root causes.
- Develop and maintain comprehensive test plans that validate mechanical performance against product requirements.
- Execute validation and verification testing, capturing both quantitative and qualitative data with high fidelity.
- Author clear, actionable test reports that summarize results, highlight risks, and recommend design or process changes.
- Partner with engineering, product, and leadership teams to inform design iterations and strategic decisions.
- Design and execute compliance and regulatory testing campaigns, informing in-house vs 3rd party testing strategy
section_requirements:

- Enjoy hands-on lab work designing, instrumenting, operating, and debugging test equipment and robotic hardware.
- Can turn evolving requirements and ambiguous failures into repeatable tests, trustworthy data, and clear engineering decisions.
- Balance rigorous validation, safety, and traceability with rapid hardware iteration.
- Communicate clearly across mechanical, electrical, software, controls, and manufacturing teams, and build alignment on risks and corrective actions.

- Experience designing test fixtures and stands using CAD, engineering drawings, and GD&T.
- Hands-on experience integrating sensors, instrumentation, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems, including calibration and measurement traceability.
- Experience developing automated or hardware-in-the-loop tests using Python, C/C++, or AI coding tools for test execution, data collection, and analysis.
- Experience designing reliability, accelerated life, environmental, and hardware qualification tests for robotic or electromechanical systems.
- Experience supporting EVT, DVT, PVT, pilot production, or sustaining hardware validation.
- Experience using root cause analysis, FMEA, or FEA to guide design improvements.
- Experience executing product standards compliance certification campaigns.

section_about:
OpenAI's Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems.
We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.
Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change.
We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.
As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes.
You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.
You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness.
Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact-not simply activity or successful demonstrations.
This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI's products evolve.
This role is based in Seoul, South Korea.

- Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.
- Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

- Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
- Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.
- Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.
- Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.
- Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

OpenAI's Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads.
Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models.
By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI's supercomputing platform.
We are seeking a Operations Program Manager (OPM) to serve as the single-threaded operational leader for new hardware introductions (NPI) and production ramps across OpenAI's AI infrastructure systems.
This role combines hands-on execution with strategic ownership.
You will be responsible for defining the operating model, aligning cross-functional stakeholders, setting the critical path, making informed tradeoffs, escalating decisively, and ensuring hardware programs deliver on schedule, quality, cost, and scalability.
Success in this role requires comfort operating in ambiguity, influencing without authority, and driving alignment across internal teams and external partners-while keeping eyes firmly on long-term system scalability and repeatability.
section_responsibilities:

- Act as the single-threaded owner for operational readiness across NPI and ramp, accountable for outcomes from early bring-up through sustained production
- Translate OpenAI's infrastructure strategy and engineering objectives into clear operating plans, execution priorities, and decision frameworks
- Drive alignment across Engineering, Operations, Strategic Sourcing, Finance, Capacity Planning, and Executive stakeholders by framing tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations
- Proactively identify inflection points where decisions or investments are required to protect long-term scale, reliability, or cost targets
- Influence operational strategy with manufacturing partners by setting expectations on execution rigor, accountability, and continuous improvement
Program Execution & Operational Excellence
- Drive overall NPI build readiness, including material accountability, manufacturing and test readiness, product data availability, factory infrastructure, and qualification plans
- Lead transition activities from NPI to mass production, partnering closely with Sustaining Operations teams to ensure seamless ownership transfer
- Translate engineering requirements into actionable, factory-ready plans with tier-1 manufacturing and integration partners
- Lead cross-functional build and debug cadences; ensure issues are clearly owned, aggressively driven, and formally closed with root cause and prevention
- Drive factory and deployment ramp readiness, including throughput, site readiness, yield targets, quality controls, and reliability gates
- Own end-to-end risk management-identification, mitigation planning, escalation, and executive-level communication
- Surface systemic bottlenecks, inefficiencies, or failure modes; propose and implement durable solutions across process, tooling, and organizational interfaces
- Build, formalize, and scale repeatable operating mechanisms that enable predictable, high-velocity hardware development
Systems, Process & Partner Leadership

- Support onsite factory builds and field deployments as needed (domestic and international travel)

- Familiarity with supplier engagement models, build cost drivers, and NPI scaling tradeoffs
- Technical background in server, rack, and/or network hardware

- Experience supporting PLM processes and familiarity with ERP systems

Our Inference team brings OpenAI's most capable research and technology to the world through our products.
We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they've never been able to before.
We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.

- Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.

- Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.

Security is foundational to OpenAI's mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.
The Security organization protects OpenAI's technology, people, and products by building and operating deeply technical systems that must work reliably at massive scale.
Our work underpins OpenAI's commitments around safety, privacy, and security across research, products, and emerging platforms.
The Host Assurance team exists to make bare metal and VMs dependable & scalable foundations for OpenAI: secure by default, verifiable in practice, and resilient across providers and operating models.
We operate at the trust boundary between hardware and cloud-scale orchestration, ensuring that hosts are eligible to safely run workloads with predictable security properties and auditability.
OpenAI is seeking a Software Engineer, Host Assurance to build and operate the services, APIs, and host software that establish and maintain trust in our compute infrastructure.
You will own production software from design and implementation through testing, rollout, observability, and operation.
Your work will support capabilities such as machine identity, certificate issuance and enrollment, secure bootstrap, and host attestation across bare-metal and VM environments.
Success in this role requires strong technical judgment, the ability to reason across software and host-system boundaries and learn unfamiliar parts of the stack, and a practical mindset for building systems that are secure, reliable, and usable in fast-moving production environments.
The systems you build will sit on the critical path of OpenAI's frontier infrastructure investments and will directly shape how large amounts of compute are brought online - securely, responsibly, and at global scale - underpinning long-lived commitments around privacy, security, and reliability.
You will partner closely with infrastructure, research, and confidential computing initiatives-including novel hardware platforms and emerging deployment models- to make the secure path the easiest path.
This role is well suited for engineers who enjoy working across trust services, operating systems, hardware and firmware validation, and infrastructure security, and who are excited by ambiguous, high-impact problems at the boundary of hardware and large-scale systems.
section_responsibilities:
- Design, build, and operate components of the Host Assurance platform that establish trust in both bare-metal & VM hosts before they are eligible for production use.

- Validate delivered hardware and firmware against vendor claims and continuously detect and manage drift over time.
- Eliminate insecure bootstrap patterns while preserving deployment throughput and operational reliability.
Partner with provisioning, fleet, and orchestration teams to deliver paved paths where the secure approach is the easiest approach.
- Own software components through implementation, operational readiness, launch, and ongoing operation.
Define readiness criteria, validate behavior under load and failure, establish monitoring and actionable alerts, plan staged rollouts and tested recovery procedures, and maintain runbooks.
Use production experience to improve reliability and reduce operational burden.
- Participate in production support via oncall rotation.
- Help define observable, testable security properties for host platforms and improve the telemetry and validation needed to enforce them in practice.
- Work across different deployment models and provider boundaries while maintaining a consistent bar for host trust outcomes.
section_requirements:
- Have strong software engineering experience building and operating reliable production systems at scale.
- Bring depth in distributed systems, backend or platform engineering, operating systems, or infrastructure security.

- Can reason across services, APIs, and host software, and learn the boot, firmware, and hardware trust mechanisms relevant to your work.

job_title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
section_about:
The Human Flourishing team's mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing.
As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people's lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities.
The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.
Our approach has two parts.
Firstly, we measure and improve models' understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people's values and to help them achieve their long-term goals.
Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.
Our recent work includes Beneficial RL which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.
We're looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior.
You'll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.
We're especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health.
Prior experience in these domains is not required.

- Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.
- Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.
- Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.
- Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

Cloud Infrastructure builds the shared platforms behind ChatGPT and the OpenAI API.

OpenAI develops and deploys AI with the goal of benefiting humanity.

job_title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer - Web Understanding and Structured Retrieval, Search
section_about:
The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI.
Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models.
We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.
The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval.
We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.
We're looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search.
You'll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneous, unstructured and semi-structured web content, making that information more accessible and useful to AI models.
The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information?
How can we extract it reliably at web scale?
And how do we measure whether it improves the model's ability to reason and answer questions?
How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?
You'll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved.
This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.

- Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.
- Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.
- Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.
- Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.

- Experience independently driving open-ended technical problems from an initial idea through experimentation and implementation.
- A first-principles approach to using AI and compute, with a willingness to rethink established methods as model capabilities improve.
- A strong interest in how the representation of information shapes what models can find, understand, and use.

section_about:
The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI's products, including ChatGPT and the API.
Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.
Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering.
We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.
You'll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI's products and services across clouds and regions.
The team's work spans L3, L4, and L7-from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.
You'll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works.
Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.
This role combines software engineering with production ownership.
You'll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.
section_responsibilities:
- Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.
- Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.
- Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.
- Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.
- Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.
- Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.
- Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.
- Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.
section_requirements:

- Have depth in one or more areas such as cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, proxies and gateways, service meshes, load balancing, or global traffic routing.
- Understand networking fundamentals and can reason about how IP routing, TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT, TLS, and HTTP/gRPC affect connectivity and performance.
- Have hands-on experience building or operating systems such as Envoy, NGINX, Istio, Cilium, or comparable networking infrastructure.
- Write production software in Go, Rust, C++, Python, or a similar language, and use software and automation to solve operational problems.
- Can investigate unfamiliar failures using evidence, test hypotheses, and follow problems through to a verified resolution.
- Take ownership of design, implementation, rollout, and ongoing reliability, and communicate clearly across teams when a problem crosses ownership boundaries.
- Care about making infrastructure secure and understandable for the engineers who depend on it.
We value deep expertise and the willingness to learn across boundaries.

section_about:
The Consumer Products team at OpenAI builds end-to-end hardware and software systems that bring AI into the physical world.
We work at the intersection of custom silicon, embedded systems, operating systems, and cloud services to deliver reliable, production-ready devices at scale.
Within Consumer Products, the camera stack is a critical sensing component.
The team partners closely with electrical engineering, silicon vendors, systems, and higher-level perception and product teams to bring up new hardware, stabilize capture pipelines, and ensure camera systems are robust, debuggable, and ready for real-world deployment.
This work spans early prototypes through production, with a strong emphasis on correctness, repeatability, and long-term reliability.
As a Camera Firmware Engineer, you will own low-level camera enablement on custom hardware-from early board bring-up through stable production capture.
You will develop and maintain the firmware and software that makes camera sensors reliable, controllable, and debuggable, forming the foundation for higher-level camera pipelines and product features.
This role is highly hands-on and systems-oriented.
You will work close to the hardware, diagnose real-world timing and integration issues, and build tooling that accelerates iteration across the entire camera stack.
We follow a hybrid work model with four days per week in the office and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
section_responsibilities:
- Bring up new camera sensors and modules on prototype and production boards, including link stability, sensor control, and correct power, reset, and clock sequencing.
- Develop and maintain low-level camera software, including sensor drivers, board configuration, and camera subsystem integration across hardware revisions.
- Enable and validate core capture paths for development and production, including RAW capture for debugging, still capture, and hardware-accelerated video encode and streaming with stable timestamps and long-duration reliability.
- Stand up camera control and repeatability features, including basic 3A loop exposure, manual overrides and locks, and deterministic presets to support validation and debugging.
- Build and maintain camera bring-up tooling, such as capture scripts, automated sweeps, manifests, and debugging utilities that make issues reproducible and easy to triage.
- Partner closely with electrical engineering, camera pipeline owners, and systems teams to define interfaces, unblock integration, and keep the camera stack stable as the device evolves.
section_requirements:
- Deep experience shipping embedded camera systems, including sensor bring-up, driver development, and board-level debugging.
- Strong C/C++ experience with embedded or Linux-based systems; comfortable debugging across kernel and userspace boundaries.
- Hands-on understanding of common camera hardware interfaces (for example, MIPI CSI and sensor control buses) and the practical realities of bring-up, including power, reset, clocking, and sequencing.
- Proven track record of building reliable capture paths and effective debug workflows that accelerate iteration through reproducible failures and well-scoped fixes.
section_preferred:
- Experience with common mobile or embedded SoC camera stacks and vendor frameworks.
- Experience integrating and debugging hardware acceleration blocks adjacent to camera pipelines, such as video encode and decode paths.
- Familiarity building higher-level capture pipelines (for example, GStreamer) on top of low-level camera enablement.

OpenAI's software footprint is expanding rapidly across SaaS, internally built tools, agents, integrations, APIs, third-party platforms, and application systems that OpenAI.
The company needs a stronger tools architecture layer that can help teams make good decisions early, avoid duplicate tools, govern sensitive data and identities, and identify where OpenAI should build instead of buy.

OpenAI's User Operations team shepherds our customers' adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional.
We are building the very first post-AGI support team.
We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products.
We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale.
OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.
We're looking for dedicated, experienced, and deeply curious individuals to help solve some of the most complex challenges faced by our customers while building the future of post-AGI support alongside us.
In this role, you'll work directly with customers through support tickets and live calls, troubleshooting high-impact issues and resolving novel, often ambiguous technical problems in one of the fastest-moving environments in technology.
As AI adoption rapidly accelerates, the work you do will directly support mission-critical systems being built on OpenAI's platform, serving as a critical line of defense for customers operating at massive scale.
Beyond resolving technical issues, you'll help define what world-class support looks like in an AGI-driven future.
You'll partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Operations to improve systems, reduce bugs, and elevate the customer experience, while leveraging automation, agents, and our own AI technology to transform how support operates at scale.

section_about:
Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world.
The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.
Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces.
We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.
We are seeking researchers to advance safety training for OpenAI's models.
You will develop methods that improve model behavior after pretraining, including RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, preference optimization, adversarial training, synthetic data generation, safety evaluations, and model behavior analysis.
This role is highly cross-functional.
You will work with core training teams, product teams, policy, legal, trust and safety, and domain experts to identify risks, design interventions, train models, evaluate outcomes, and launch safety improvements in OpenAI products.
section_responsibilities:
- Conduct research on safety post-training methods, including RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling, adversarial training, synthetic data, and scalable oversight
- Develop and implement model training interventions that make models safer, more reliable, and more aligned with user intent
- Build evaluations and measurement infrastructure for safety harms, high-stakes reliability failures, policy adherence, jailbreak robustness, multimodal risks, agent behavior, and domain-specific risks
- Translate ambiguous safety problems into concrete research plans, datasets, training runs, evals, and product-facing improvements
- Analyze model failures such as hallucination, unsafe tool use, prompt injection, privacy leakage, over-refusal, under-refusal, sycophancy, and deceptive or misleading behavior
- Partner with domain experts to design safety training approaches for areas like cyber, privacy, youth safety, wellbeing, and other frontier-risk domains
- Collaborate with research and deployment teams to ensure safety improvements are incorporated into OpenAI's core model training and product launches
section_requirements:
- Have hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or post-training language models, multimodal models, or agentic systems
- Have experience with RL, RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling, preference optimization, instruction tuning, or related post-training methods
- Care deeply about shaping model behavior in real-world systems, not only publishing research
- Are excited by open-ended safety problems where the right method, dataset, eval, or training objective may not be obvious at the start
- Bring strong research judgment and strong engineering ability, including comfort running experiments, analyzing model behavior, and working with large-scale ML systems
- Have experience in one or more relevant domains: agents, tool use, multimodal models, cyber/security, reliability, uncertainty calibration, factuality, evals, privacy, youth safety, wellbeing, or applied alignment
- Enjoy collaborating across research, engineering, product, policy, legal, and trust and safety teams
- Hold a PhD in machine learning, computer science, or a related field, or have equivalent practical research or engineering experience
section_preferred:
- Experience improving production model behavior through post-training or deployment feedback
- Experience building safety evals, automated graders, red-teaming systems, or monitoring pipelines
- Experience working with human feedback, expert feedback, synthetic data, or policy-grounded training data
- Experience in safety-critical or abuse-sensitive domains where models must balance helpfulness, refusal, uncertainty, and user intent

job_title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Equipment
section_about:
OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads.
The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.
We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning.
Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.
As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer, you will oversee the quality of data center equipment at supplier factories.
You will use production data, audits, and test results to identify systemic, recurring, or safety-related issues and work with suppliers to address them through Closed Loop Learning (CLL).
You will work with suppliers and internal teams to define inspections and factory tests for each type of equipment.
You will coordinate issue resolution before shipment and manage deviations across multiple suppliers and project sites.
section_responsibilities:
Manufacturing Monitoring and Supplier Improvement
- Manufacturing monitoring: Work with Manufacturing Operations to monitor production progress, quality controls, inspection results, and test readiness.
Flag emerging risks and coordinate a response with suppliers.
- Product and process audits: Audit products and processes during and after production against engineering requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, approved procedures, and quality standards.
Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.
- Manufacturing coordination: Agree on production checkpoints and inspection and testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams.
Escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.
- Manufacturing scorecards: Develop supplier and product scorecards with Manufacturing Operations.
Review audit findings, test results, recurring defects, and open issues with suppliers to prioritize improvements.
- Drive continuous improvement: Lead the CLL process with suppliers.
Track root cause analyses and corrective and preventive actions in a shared register.
Verify that each action addresses the underlying problem before closing it.
Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)
- Standardize requirements and formats: Develop product-specific FAT requirements and standard test formats with equipment suppliers and OpenAI's engineering, commissioning, quality, and Manufacturing Operations teams.
- Define critical quality requirements: Document the CTQ characteristics each test must verify in an OpenAI-accepted format.
Use CLL findings to revise FAT procedures so future tests check for known failure modes.
- Ensure auditable supplier records: Require suppliers to retain test results and make them available for OpenAI audits.
- Manage documentation and revision control: Review final FAT records and audit reports for each piece of equipment and maintain a controlled revision history.
- Conduct periodic supplier audits: Check that suppliers follow approved test procedures and that their records accurately reflect the tests performed.
Factory Witness Testing (FWT)
- Align checklists and stakeholders: Develop standard FWT checklists with OpenAI subject matter experts, installing contractors, and the construction management team.
Agree on requirements before testing begins.
- Manage documentation and reporting: Collect and review final witness test reports and supporting records from participants.
- Before shipment, confirm that each witness-test issue is resolved or covered by a documented deviation.
Log systemic, recurring, or safety-related findings in the CLL tracker and verify the effectiveness of corrective actions with the supplier.
Deviation Management
- Assess short shipments and missing or failed tests in partnership with Manufacturing Operations.
- Coordinate supplier support to resolve issues at the project site.
- Document each deviation and track the agreed actions through closure.
section_requirements:
- Bachelor's degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.
- At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and project management.
- Experience coordinating FAT and FWT with suppliers and resolving equipment quality issues.
- Ability to develop test checklists, define CTQs, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.
- Experience monitoring supplier production, auditing products and processes during and after production, and using scorecards to improve supplier and product quality.
Experience managing controlled documents and deviations.
- Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple pieces of equipment.
- Ability to communicate quality requirements and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, and construction teams.
- Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40-60% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.
section_preferred:

- Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.
- ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.
- PMP or equivalent project management certification.
- Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.

We're looking for a Product Reliability Engineer to own reliability engineering for advanced IT hardware, from printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) through compute and networking trays, systems, and fully integrated racks.
You'll translate operating conditions and service-life goals into reliability requirements, design and execute qualification tests, and drive failure analysis and corrective-action verification from development through production and field deployment.
Working with electrical, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, quality, and data center teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you'll use test and field evidence to improve hardware durability, serviceability, and availability.
section_responsibilities:
- Define reliability requirements and targets for PCBAs, trays, systems, and racks using mission profiles, expected service life, operating environments, duty cycles, and availability goals.
- Drive design-for-reliability reviews with electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineers.
Use failure modes and effects analysis (DFMEA or FMEA) and physics of failure to prioritize risks and recommend design improvements.
Own component de-rating guidelines and guidance.
- Own reliability qualification plans from new product introduction through production, defining test coverage, representative configurations, sample sizes, stress conditions, duration, pass/fail criteria, and exit evidence at each assembly level.
- Develop and execute accelerated life and environmental tests, including temperature cycling, humidity exposure, power cycling, shock, vibration, and transport testing.
Exercise hardware under representative workloads and monitor function and degradation during stress.
- Analyze life-test and field data using Weibull and other reliability models, acceleration models, and confidence intervals.
State assumptions, exposure, and uncertainty when estimating failure rates, useful life, or reliability against targets.
- Lead failure investigations from symptom reproduction through physical root cause.
Maintain failure reporting, analysis, and corrective-action records, and verify fixes through targeted testing and recurrence monitoring.
- Review supplier reliability plans and evidence for PCBs, PCBa components/assemblies, cables, connectors, and cooling components.
Identify gaps between component qualification and the stresses encountered in the integrated system or rack.
- Work hands-on with internal and partner labs to develop fixtures, instrumentation, and test methods.
Review sample traceability, test configurations, calibration, raw data, and failure capture, including on-site support at manufacturing partners.
- Partner with manufacturing and quality engineers to establish and validate reliability screens, burn-in where justified, and ongoing reliability testing.
Confirm screening detects relevant defects without consuming unacceptable product life.
- Evaluate reliability risks introduced by assembly and integration: board strain and solder-joint damage, connector mating and retention, cable routing, fastener preload, power connections, and thermal interfaces.
Partner with cooling specialists on leak integrity, material compatibility, corrosion, and cooling performance over life.
- Plan reliability test resources, lab capacity, hardware samples, schedules, and dependencies across programs with engineering teams, technical program managers, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.
- Present qualification results, unresolved failure modes, and residual risk at design and release reviews.
Make evidence-based readiness recommendations and clearly identify test gaps, required follow-up, and decisions for accountable owners.
- Assess reliability impact and define targeted requalification for design, component, supplier, manufacturing process, and repair changes, including firmware changes that alter hardware operating stresses.
- Track field returns and fleet failure trends with service and data center teams.
Correlate telemetry, failure analysis, and configuration history to prioritize corrective actions and feed lessons into future designs and qualification plans.
- Validate serviceability and repeated assembly or maintenance operations, including connector mating cycles and component replacement.
Work with system engineers to assess how hardware failures, redundancy, and recovery affect rack availability.
section_requirements:
- Have hands-on reliability engineering experience with advanced IT hardware, such as AI/HPC servers, networking equipment, or storage systems, spanning PCBAs, electromechanical assemblies, and integrated racks.
- Have designed, instrumented, and executed hardware reliability tests, debugged failures in the lab, and translated results into practical design or process improvements.
- Understand failure mechanisms in electronic assemblies, including solder fatigue, PCB and laminate damage, connector wear, corrosion, and thermal or mechanical degradation.
- Can turn mission profiles and failure risks into qualification plans, select defensible sample sizes and stress levels, and explain the assumptions and limits of accelerated testing.
- Have led reliability qualification through development and production milestones, balancing sample availability, lab capacity, schedule, and the evidence needed for release decisions.
- Have worked directly with component suppliers, joint design manufacturers, contract manufacturers, and external test labs to review test methods, resolve failures, and verify corrective actions.
- Apply design for reliability, DFMEA, and physics-of-failure methods across electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces, and understand how manufacturing, assembly, handling, and repair affect long-term reliability.
- Have driven structured failure analysis and corrective action using methods such as 8D, supported by electrical diagnostics, microscopy, X-ray, cross-section analysis, or specialist failure-analysis labs as appropriate.
- Can analyze reliability and life-test data, including censored data, Weibull distributions, and confidence bounds, using tools such as Python, R, JMP, or equivalent statistical software.
- Bring experience with high-power electronics, dense interconnects, or liquid-cooled hardware, including thermal interfaces, leak integrity, material compatibility, and serviceability.
- Communicate technical findings and uncertainty clearly, distinguish verified root cause and corrective-action effectiveness from hypotheses, and prioritize reliability risks when requirements or designs change.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you'll use your deep understanding of OpenAI's infrastructure and products, together with each customer's architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time.
You'll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents.
Success means that as a customer's workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.
section_responsibilities:
- Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.
- Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain.
Where possible, you'll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you'll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering's investigation.
- Become a trusted expert on OpenAI's products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.
- Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents.
You'll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.
- Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.
- Develop a detailed understanding of each customer's architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints.
You'll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.
- Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.
- Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.
- Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.
- Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.
- Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.
- Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.
- Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.
- Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.
section_requirements:

- Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.
- Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.
- Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

- Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders-especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

- Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

section_about:
OpenAI's mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.
We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI.
The Global Affairs team builds trusted relationships that help external stakeholders understand advanced AI and ensure that their perspectives inform our work.
Within Global Affairs, the National Security Policy team works across OpenAI to understand how increasingly capable AI systems affect security, governance, and democratic resilience, and to advance policies that support the responsible development and use of AI.
OpenAI is seeking a highly organized and skilled Program Manager, National Security Policy Operations to join the Global Affairs team, reporting directly to Sasha Baker, who leads the National Security Policy team.
This is a hands-on program management role focused on running the planning, coordination, and execution systems that enable the team to operate effectively.
This person will translate team priorities into executable plans, synthesize data and inputs into clear program updates, manage key programs and workstreams, and create the operating discipline that keeps decisions, dependencies, and follow-through on track.
This role sits at the center of the National Security Policy team's planning, prioritization, information flow, and execution.
Success means giving the team clear visibility into commitments, dependencies, decisions, and risks; reducing fragmented operational work; enabling faster and better-informed decisions; and ensuring priorities move reliably from scoping through completion.
The ideal candidate takes deep pride in program management as a craft and is energized by enabling policy and technical experts to do their best work.
The role works closely with policy experts but is not primarily responsible for setting policy positions or serving as the team's external policy lead.
This role may be based in San Francisco or Washington, DC.
It will require travel as necessary,
and we offer relocation assistance to new employees.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE:
- Run portfolio planning and team operations, including intake, workplans, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and progress reporting.
Surface capacity constraints, recommend sequencing and tradeoffs, and escalate decisions to the team lead, who sets priorities and makes resource decisions.
- Build and maintain lightweight, repeatable operating systems for planning, meeting cadences, knowledge management, decision logs, and centralized tracking of developments, commitments, and follow-up.
- Own the team's program metrics and central tracking of commitments, owners, deadlines, dependencies, decisions, and follow-up.
Keep records current and reliable, and produce concise updates and practical dashboards that make progress, risks, and decisions clear to policy leaders.
- Coordinate policy deliverables and external engagements from planning through follow-up.
Assemble briefing packages; draft talking points, presentations, readouts, and updates; organize visits and convenings, including logistics; manage review cycles; and track action items through completion, with substantive input and approval from policy leads.
- Own operational management of the team's contractors and consultants, coordinating onboarding, scopes of work, deliverables, contract renewals, invoices, and offboarding with Legal, Finance, Procurement, and other relevant teams.
Track commitments and performance against agreed deliverables, and flag issues requiring the team lead's decision.
- Coordinate across Global Affairs, Research, Safety, Security, Product Policy, Legal, Communications, and OpenAI for Government to manage dependencies, surface decisions, and advance shared priorities.
- Continuously improve the team's operating model through feedback loops, retrospectives, and thoughtful use of AI, automation, and lightweight tooling.
YOU SHOULD THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:
- Enjoy learning enough technical and policy context to coordinate work effectively and synthesize expert inputs into clear briefing materials and updates for technical and non-technical audiences.
- Thrive in fast-paced, flexible environments where priorities evolve and good judgment matters.
- Collaborate effectively across policy, technical, legal, operational, and business teams.
- Can lead complex workstreams and keep stakeholders aligned through influence rather than formal authority.
- View program management as a craft in its own right and take satisfaction in building durable systems, creating clarity, and helping teams deliver reliably.
- Are passionate about the promise of AI and thoughtful about its potential national security and societal risks.
- Are energized by enabling subject-matter experts and leaders to do their best work, and bring high standards, low ego, curiosity, and a strong service orientation.
WE'RE LOOKING FOR A BLEND OF:
- 5+ years of relevant experience in program management, project management, policy operations, strategic operations, chief of staff, government program delivery, or related roles.
- Experience coordinating complex work across multiple stakeholders and building practical systems that help teams deliver.
Experience supporting policy, government, national security, or technical teams is a plus.
- A track record of independently driving complex cross-functional programs from scoping through delivery, managing stakeholders, dependencies, and risks while building durable systems and delivering measurable outcomes.
- Strong analytical, writing, and communication skills, with the ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative inputs into crisp decision materials, action plans, and executive-ready updates.
- The ability to understand strategic context while remaining hands-on in detailed execution, influence without formal authority, and exercise sound judgment and discretion in fast-moving, sensitive environments.
- Genuine care for the impact of AI on national security, democratic institutions, and society; familiarity with areas such as frontier risk, cybersecurity, biosecurity, critical infrastructure, defense and intelligence applications, or technical AI governance is a plus.
Formal project or program management certification is welcome but not required.

OpenAI's Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems.
For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle-transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.
We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations.
We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.
As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed.
You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.
You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems-often using Codex itself as part of your development process.
You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

Our work spans coding, tool use, computer use, multi-agent coordination, long-horizon execution, factuality, instruction following, calibrated reasoning, and taste.
Our team is where new model capabilities get made.

section_about:
OpenAI's Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads.
Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models.
By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI's supercomputing platform.
OpenAI is developing custom silicon to power the next generation of frontier AI models.
We're looking for experienced Design Verification (DV) Engineers to ensure functional correctness and robust design for our cutting-edge ML accelerators.
You will play a key role in verifying complex hardware systems-ranging from individual IP blocks to subsystems and full SoC-working closely with architecture, RTL, software, and systems teams to deliver reliable silicon at scale.
section_responsibilities:
- Own the verification of one or more of: custom IP blocks, subsystems (compute, interconnect, memory, etc.), or full-chip SoC-level functionality.
- Define verification plans based on architecture and microarchitecture specs.
- Develop constrained-random, directed, and system-level testbenches using SystemVerilog/UVM or equivalent methodologies.
- Build and maintain stimulus generators, checkers, monitors, and scoreboards to ensure high coverage and correctness.
- Drive bug triage, root cause analysis, and work closely with design teams on resolution.
- Contribute to regression infrastructure, coverage analysis, and closure for both block- and top-level environments.
section_requirements:
- BS/MS in EE/CE/CS or equivalent with 3+ years of experience in hardware verification.
- Proven success verifying complex IP or SoC designs in industry-standard flows
- Proficient in SystemVerilog, UVM, and common simulation and debug tools (e.g., VCS, Questa, Verdi).
- Strong knowledge of computer architecture concepts, memory and cache systems, coherency, interconnects, and/or ML compute primitives.
- Familiarity with performance modeling, formal verification, or emulation is a plus.
- Experience working in fast-paced, cross-disciplinary teams with a passion for building reliable hardware.
To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

REW's scope spans portfolio strategy, design and construction, space planning, sustainability, workplace experience, and global operations.
